summary: Backend + frontend e2e validation of the new PERSONAL MEMORY and MUSIC/AMBIANCE commands (iteration 4). Backend 15/15 (5 new memory tests + 10 regression). Frontend: setup, memory save (regex catches 'souviens-toi que ...'), memory recall, memory persists across reload and is sent in /api/chat body (Groq references lasagnes), music generic (window.open to youtube.com/results?search_query=musique%20playlist%20tendance), music relax (-> ambiance%20relaxante%20lofi), and no-false-trigger on 'raconte une blague' all pass. ONE minor regex robustness bug found in the memory-RECALL client-side intent (apostrophe-only variant), see action_items.

integration_issues.issue: After clearing memory, asking 'qu est-ce que tu sais sur moi' (without apostrophe, as specified in the review request) does NOT hit the client-side memory-recall regex (which requires "qu'est-ce" with apostrophe). The query falls through to /api/chat which still has the prior conversation history in MongoDB (sirius_chats.history) containing the lasagnes fact, so the brain answers as if memory still existed. UX result: user just told Sirius to forget, but Sirius still references the old fact via chat history. Two complementary fixes recommended: (1) loosen recall regex to also match the apostrophe-less form (e.g. "qu['’ ]est[- ]ce que tu sais", "que sais tu"); (2) on memory-clear, also POST /api/chat with a system-reset signal OR clear the per-session history server-side (e.g. DELETE /api/chat/session/{id}).

action_items: App.js processCommand (line ~589): broaden memory-recall regex to also match apostrophe-less / hyphen-less variants: e.g. /qu['’ ]?est[- ]?ce que tu sais (sur|de) moi|que sais[- ]?tu (sur|de) moi/i. Same hardening could be applied to the memory-clear and music regex families.

Optional: on memory-clear, also reset the backend session history. Add an endpoint like POST /api/chat/reset {session_id} that does db.sirius_chats.delete_one({session_id}); frontend calls it inside the saveMemory([]) branch. Otherwise old memory facts persist in MongoDB history and bleed into future answers.
critical_code_review_comments: App.js (line 11): hard-coded WS_URL='ws://localhost:8765' still produces a console error on every load in the cloud preview. Gate behind an env flag (e.g. REACT_APP_ENABLE_LOCAL_WS) for distributed builds.
App.js processCommand (line ~589) memory-recall regex relies on a typed apostrophe; review_request and STT often drop it. See action_items.

server.py /api/chat persists every user+assistant pair (last 16) but exposes no reset endpoint, so 'oublie tout' is only client-side. The backend history (last 6 turns reinjected into the prompt) defeats the memory-clear illusion.
sirius_brain.build_system_prompt still does not sanitize newlines/markdown in profile.interests or memory entries — low-risk prompt-injection vector for a distributed app.
App.js cloudAnswer useCallback (line ~542) lists `memory` in its dep array but actually reads `memoryRef.current` — the dep is unused (no bug, just dead dep; could be removed for clarity).
App.js openMusic: window.open with `_blank` is correctly used; in browser preview popup blockers may suppress it silently — Electron build will not have this issue.

success_rate.frontend: 87.5% (7/8 — memory save, recall, persist+brain, music generic, music relax, no-false-trigger, memory-clear erases localStorage and shows confirmation; FAIL: post-clear recall still references old fact via backend history + apostrophe regex)

context_for_next_testing_agent: localStorage keys: sirius_profile, sirius_keys, sirius_memory (array of strings), sirius_eco. Memory/music/clear are CLIENT-side regex in App.js processCommand (lines 569-639) BEFORE any LLM call. Backend ChatRequest now has `memory: list = []` passed into sirius_brain.build_system_prompt under section 'CE QUE TU SAIS DÉJÀ SUR L'UTILISATEUR'. KEY GOTCHA for next tester: the subtitle goes through an intermediate state 'Vous : « <command> »' while thinking, so polling should ignore that prefix and wait for the real answer (up to ~15s for cloud calls). Use window.open stub + speechSynthesis.speak no-op to avoid popups/audio. The post-clear recall failure is a real UX bug, see action_items.
rca of the issue: Step 1: enter setup with profile {name:Daniel} + groq key. Step 2: 'souviens-toi que j adore les lasagnes' -> regex catches, localStorage['sirius_memory']=['j adore les lasagnes'], subtitle 'C’est noté : j adore les lasagnes.'. Step 3: 'oublie tout' -> regex catches, saveMemory([]), localStorage emptied, subtitle 'C’est fait, j’ai effacé tout ce que je savais sur vous.'. Step 4: 'qu est-ce que tu sais sur moi' (NO apostrophe per review_request spec) -> client recall regex /qu'est-ce que tu sais sur moi|.../ does NOT match because the literal ' is absent -> request falls through to keys.groq branch -> POST /api/chat with memory=[] BUT session_id unchanged -> server reads sirius_chats.history (still contains 'j adore les lasagnes' from earlier turns) -> Groq answers 'Daniel, je sais juste que ton plat préféré est les lasagnes...'. Mitigation: (a) loosen recall regex to accept ' or apostrophe variants, (b) reset server-side history when memory is cleared, or (c) include a session_id rotation on clear. The first two fixes are tiny and self-contained.
